item.title: Augusta Avenue Bridge Closes Nov. 10 for Rehabilitation Work
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County's Construction Management Division will shut down the Augusta Avenue Bridge to through traffic starting Tuesday, Nov. 10, for a comprehensive rehabilitation project on the bridge's existing structure. The closure is expected to last through December 2026, barring weather delays or other construction complications. Drivers will be…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County's Construction Management Division will shut down the Augusta Avenue Bridge to through traffic starting Tuesday, Nov. 10, for a comprehensive rehabilitation project on the bridge's existing structure. The closure is expected to last through December 2026, barring weather delays or other construction complications.

Drivers will be detoured to Atlanta Avenue and Selma Avenue during the work. The county urges motorists to exercise caution in the work zone and follow posted signs and road crew instructions. While the bridge itself will be closed to traffic, residents, pedestrians, local traffic, and emergency vehicles will retain access to properties within the work area, though some driveways and entrances may be temporarily blocked as crews move equipment and materials.

Construction schedules can shift due to weather or logistics, so the county advises drivers to check for updates before the closure takes effect.

item.title: Pensacola Woman Charged with Murder in Stabbing Initially Called Self-Inflicted
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Pensacola woman was arrested Tuesday on a murder charge following a stabbing that authorities initially believed was self-inflicted, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office. Deputies arrested 29-year-old Kordaja Lakita Smith on November 4th and charged her with second-degree murder in connection with the fatal stabbing. The case…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola woman was arrested Tuesday on a murder charge following a stabbing that authorities initially believed was self-inflicted, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies arrested 29-year-old Kordaja Lakita Smith on November 4th and charged her with second-degree murder in connection with the fatal stabbing. The case represents a significant shift in the investigation after the incident was originally classified as self-inflicted.

The ECSO has not yet released additional details about the circumstances of the stabbing, the victim's identity, or what prompted investigators to reconsider their initial assessment. The arrest comes as detectives continue their investigation into the deadly incident.

item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County finished fiscal year 2025-2026 with more than $2 million in operational surplus, according to County Clerk and Comptroller Jason English.

The surplus represents unspent funds remaining after the county's operational budget cycle ended. County officials typically use such surpluses for contingencies, capital projects, or reserve accounts that help stabilize future budget planning.

English's report comes as local governments throughout Northwest Florida manage their finances heading into the new fiscal year.

item.title: Area high schools wrap up week with decisive football wins
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Several North Escambia and surrounding area high schools saw action this week, with dominant performances across the board. On Wednesday night, Blountstown dominated Northview 34-6, while Marianna edged Jay 24-20 in a closer contest. Pace narrowly defeated Niceville 30-25 in another tight matchup. Tuesday's slate featured some more lopsided…
item.content:encoded:
Several North Escambia and surrounding area high schools saw action this week, with dominant performances across the board.

On Wednesday night, Blountstown dominated Northview 34-6, while Marianna edged Jay 24-20 in a closer contest. Pace narrowly defeated Niceville 30-25 in another tight matchup.

Tuesday's slate featured some more lopsided scores. Tate overwhelmed Navarre 55-7, and Escambia shut out Gulf Breeze 30-0. Milton squeaked past Washington 14-12, while Pine Forest dominated Pensacola 40-0. South Walton also posted a shutout victory over West Florida, winning 28-0.

item.content:encoded:
The Century Lions Club has rescheduled its Cross Country 5K Run/Walk for the second time, moving the event from this Saturday, November 7, to spring 2027.

The postponement comes because youth football playoffs are taking over Anthony Pleasant Park this weekend, leaving no venue for the race. The event was originally planned for October 10 before Hurricane Isaias forced an initial reschedule to November.

Century residents and participants should mark their calendars for a spring date to be announced by the Lions Club.

item.title: Century Council votes tonight on water system upgrade financing plan
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Century Town Council is set to hold a public hearing and special meeting this evening to consider a key step forward for the town's water infrastructure. Council members will vote on Resolution 2026-010, which would formally approve and adopt Century's Water Facility Plan under the Florida Department of Environmental Protection State Revolving…
item.content:encoded:
The Century Town Council is set to hold a public hearing and special meeting this evening to consider a key step forward for the town's water infrastructure. Council members will vote on Resolution 2026-010, which would formally approve and adopt Century's Water Facility Plan under the Florida Department of Environmental Protection State Revolving Fund program — a state financing mechanism designed to help municipalities pay for water system improvements.

The resolution, if approved, would clear the way for the town to pursue grant and loan funding through the SRF program to support planned upgrades to Century's municipal water system. Details on the specific scope and cost of the proposed improvements have not yet been disclosed.

The public hearing is scheduled for tonight. Residents interested in the water facility plan or who wish to comment on the resolution are encouraged to attend.

item.content:encoded:
Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Wednesday he will call a special legislative session within the next two months to implement a property tax reduction that Florida voters approved at the ballot box Tuesday evening.

DeSantis made the statement to reporters following the electoral win. The governor did not provide specific details about the timing or scope of the special session, but indicated it would be convened to put into law the tax cut measure that passed with voter approval.

The property tax reduction is likely to affect homeowners and property owners across Florida, including here in Northwest Florida. Implementation details — such as effective dates and how the cut will be administered — will likely be worked out during the special session.

item.title: Cold Front Brings Cooler Weekend to Pensacola Area
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Highs will drop from the lower 80s today into the 70s by Friday and Saturday. Sunday is expected to be the coolest day of the stretch, with highs bottoming…
item.content:encoded:
A cold front moving through the region Thursday will usher in noticeably cooler and drier conditions for the weekend and into early next week, according to North Escambia weather forecasting.

Highs will drop from the lower 80s today into the 70s by Friday and Saturday. Sunday is expected to be the coolest day of the stretch, with highs bottoming out around 68 degrees.

The shift marks a departure from the warmth earlier this week and sets up more comfortable fall conditions heading into the final days of the first week of November.

item.content:encoded:

Representatives will staff Century Town Hall from 10 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on both November 6 and 7, offering utility bill assistance and other storm-related relief to eligible residents.

The mobile assistance is part of ongoing recovery efforts following recent hurricane impact in the North Escambia area. Residents struggling with utility costs or other recovery needs from storm damage are encouraged to stop by during those hours. CAPC staff will assess eligibility and help connect residents with available aid programs.

For residents unable to visit during those times or seeking more information about services, contacting CAPC directly is recommended.

item.content:encoded:
The Blue Angels are set to perform at NAS Pensacola this Friday and Saturday for the base's Blue Angels Homecoming Airshow, coinciding with the 200th anniversary of the installation. According to WKRG News 5, Navy personnel have been preparing the base for the event, setting up chairs, tables, tents, and other infrastructure to accommodate crowds of spectators.

The airshow marks a significant milestone for NAS Pensacola, which has served as a key military aviation hub for two centuries. The Blue Angels, the Navy's elite flight demonstration squadron based at the Pensacola base, will headline the weekend event with their signature high-speed aerial maneuvers.

Details on airshow hours, gate access, parking, and other logistics for attendees have not been confirmed in available reports. Those planning to attend are advised to check the official NAS Pensacola website or contact the base directly for more information.

item.title: Escambia County 2026 property tax bills mailed; Amendment 3 changes start in 2027
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Tax Collector's Office has mailed out 2026 property tax bills, and Tax Collector Scott Lunsford is reminding property owners that those bills are accurate and due as printed — changes from Amendment 3 won't take effect until next year. Amendment 3, which Florida voters approved, will significantly increase homestead exemptions,…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Tax Collector's Office has mailed out 2026 property tax bills, and Tax Collector Scott Lunsford is reminding property owners that those bills are accurate and due as printed — changes from Amendment 3 won't take effect until next year.

Amendment 3, which Florida voters approved, will significantly increase homestead exemptions, but the full benefit won't arrive immediately. The homestead exemption will jump from $50,000 (in effect January 1, 2026) to $150,000 on January 1, 2027, and then to $250,000 on January 1, 2028. Because Florida collects property taxes after the tax year they cover, this year's bills reflect only 2026 law.

"We understand the passage of Amendment 3 has raised questions about property taxes, especially as property owners receive their 2026 tax bills," Lunsford said. "The important thing to remember is that Amendment 3 takes effect beginning with the 2027 tax year. Your 2026 property tax bill is accurate, and the amount owed remains due and payable."

Property owners can save money by paying early. Those paying in November get a 4% discount, dropping to 3% in December, 2% in January, and 1% in February. The full amount is due by March 31, with taxes becoming delinquent April 1, 2027. Bills can be viewed and paid online at EscambiaTaxCollector.com.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola has opened a Disaster Multi-Agency Resource Center at Brownsville Community Center, located at 3200 W. Desoto Street, to help residents recover from Hurricane Isaias. The center provides access to storm-related resources and assistance in one location.

The resource center closes at 7 p.m. today, Wednesday, and will operate from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily beginning Thursday, according to a city announcement. Meanwhile, FEMA registration points are closing today, so residents seeking federal disaster assistance should apply now if they haven't already.

Residents needing help with recovery efforts can visit the Brownsville Community Center during operating hours. For more information, contact the City of Pensacola Public Information Office at 850-435-1629.

item.title: Florida Lottery Urges Adults to Keep Lottery Tickets Away From Children This Holiday Season
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As the holiday shopping season kicks off, the Florida Lottery is reminding gift-givers that lottery tickets are entertainment products for adults only, not children. The Florida Lottery has joined the National Council on Problem Gambling's annual "Gift Responsibly" campaign, which runs through the end of the year. The effort aims to educate…
item.content:encoded:
As the holiday shopping season kicks off, the Florida Lottery is reminding gift-givers that lottery tickets are entertainment products for adults only, not children.

The Florida Lottery has joined the National Council on Problem Gambling's annual "Gift Responsibly" campaign, which runs through the end of the year. The effort aims to educate Floridians about the risks of youth gambling and encourage responsible gift-giving practices during November and December. Florida Lottery Secretary Reginald D. Dixon said in a statement that lottery games "are designed to be entertainment for adults, and it's important that we keep them that way."

Florida law prohibits lottery ticket sales to anyone under 18. The Gaming Control Commission and the Lottery plan to share educational messages across social media throughout the holiday season, emphasizing that lottery products belong in adults' hands only. The campaign is part of a broader, multi-state effort organized by the National Council on Problem Gambling and supported by the North American Association of State and Provincial Lotteries.

For resources on responsible play, Floridians can visit floridalottery.com/play-responsibly.

item.title: Orlando Airport Lands Historic Air Taxi at Nation's First Commercial Vertipad
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida achieved another milestone in advanced aviation technology Wednesday as Joby Aviation successfully completed a test flight at Orlando International Airport, landing an electric air taxi at the nation's first dedicated vertipad built at a commercial airport. The demonstration marks the second major flight in Florida's Future of Flight…
item.content:encoded:
Florida achieved another milestone in advanced aviation technology Wednesday as Joby Aviation successfully completed a test flight at Orlando International Airport, landing an electric air taxi at the nation's first dedicated vertipad built at a commercial airport. The demonstration marks the second major flight in Florida's Future of Flight Series and represents a significant step toward integrating flying cars into the state's transportation network.

The vertipad at MCO is purpose-built infrastructure designed specifically for electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs. According to Joby's Chief Policy Officer Greg Bowles, the project required two years of simulator testing to prove that air taxis could safely operate in the airspace around a major commercial airport without disrupting regular flight operations. "Today we demonstrated how quiet, electric, vertical lift aircraft can integrate into existing airspace," Bowles said.

Florida is participating in the Federal Aviation Administration's eVTOL and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Pilot Program, which is gathering real-world data to help the FAA develop regulations and procedures for commercial flying car service. The state has identified the Interstate 4 corridor between Orlando and Tampa as a primary route for initial commercial deployment. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue called the achievement proof that "strategic investments in infrastructure can support the safe integration of emerging aircraft into our transportation system."

The successful landing at MCO follows Florida's first AAM test flight in late October, which recreated a historic 1914 commercial airline flight using next-generation aircraft. Officials say the vertipad and infrastructure development position Florida to launch the nation's first commercial air taxi services.

item.title: Santa Rosa County opens MARC, weekend FEMA assistance hours for Hurricane Isaias recovery
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is reopening a Multi-Agency Resource Center on Friday with expanded weekend hours to help residents navigate disaster recovery following Hurricane Isaias. The center will operate 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily at the Santa Rosa County Administrative Complex Boardroom, 6495 Caroline Street in Milton. When the boardroom is in use for…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is reopening a Multi-Agency Resource Center on Friday with expanded weekend hours to help residents navigate disaster recovery following Hurricane Isaias.

The center will operate 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily at the Santa Rosa County Administrative Complex Boardroom, 6495 Caroline Street in Milton. When the boardroom is in use for meetings, the MARC will relocate to the lobby area. The reopening is supported by the Florida Division of Emergency Management and federal agencies.

Residents can meet face-to-face with representatives from the State of Florida, FEMA, and the U.S. Small Business Administration without an appointment. The county has also set up dedicated FEMA Individual Assistance registration points at two locations — the Administrative Complex hallway and Bray-Hendricks Park in Jay — both open Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Additional locations may open as recovery efforts continue.

Santa Rosa County has received a FEMA Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, making residents who suffered Hurricane Isaias damage eligible to apply for housing grants, home repairs, low-interest loans, and other relief programs. Residents can apply online at DisasterAssistance.gov, by phone at 1-800-621-3362, or through the FEMA mobile app. FEMA recommends filing insurance claims first before applying for federal assistance.
